title: Choose the visual world for ramondeleonca
question: Three full directions for the portfolio, each with a first-screen sketch. Keep Match Day, take another, or re-roll for a fresh hand.

options.label: Match Day
options.lineage: FRC event webcast and its on-screen score bar
options.thesis: The site is a match on air, and the score bar is the navigation.
materials: match video printed in one ink
options.viewport: Full-bleed match video in blue, one sentence over it, and a pinned score bar: projects in the blue block, a 2:30 clock that runs as you scroll, contact in the red block.
options.risk: Can read as a sports gimmick to web clients who have never watched an FRC match.

raised.raise: Two inks only, blue and red, with their overlap as the third; every photo is printed as a duotone instead of full colour.
Flat colour with no gradients or glow, and every element sized in whole score-bar units.
One project list drives the score bar, the match schedule and each project page.
Nothing moves unless the visitor moves: the clock runs on scroll, never on a timer.
Language and section changes announce themselves in the score bar, with no extra pop-ups or badges.

options.label: Field Manual
options.lineage: FRC and MechaLeague game manuals and their top-down field drawings
options.thesis: The field drawing is the site map, and a planned robot path drives you through it.
options.viewport: Name and one paragraph on the left; on the right a top-down field where each zone is a project and a yellow path links them.
options.risk: The most expected look for a robotics student, and a field diagram means little to a web client.

options.label: Faja
options.lineage: Tokyo record sleeve wrapped in a paper obi band
options.thesis: One project alone on a pale page, and a pink band under it carrying the whole CV.
options.viewport: One project photo on an almost empty page; a rosa mexicano band across the bottom third holds name, roles, awards and contact, and slides away to show the project.
options.case: Fuses well: an obi exists to carry the translation and credits, which is a bilingual CV. Loses on recognition, since neither audience knows the object.
options.risk: Depends on a few excellent photos, and the dense band needs a different form on phones.

options.label: Two-Ink Print
options.thesis: Everything printed in two spot inks that misregister where they meet.
options.viewport: Cut-paper shapes and a bold name in pink and blue, slightly out of register.
options.case: Warm paper and zine texture belong to print culture, not to a robotics pit or a client meeting.
options.kept: Limited-ink discipline: two colours and their overlap do all the work.
options.risk: A look many portfolios already wear.

options.label: Teletext Pages
options.thesis: The portfolio as numbered broadcast pages built from colour blocks.
options.viewport: Page 100 index with projects as numbered rows in flat colour.
options.case: Teletext never aired in Mexico, and typing page numbers slows a recruiter with one minute.
options.kept: Total palette commitment and a strict cell grid.
options.risk: Retro novelty that hides photos of the actual robots.

options.label: Tension Column
options.thesis: Projects and skills as rods and cords holding each other up.
options.viewport: A column of struts with each project pinned to a node on a leader line.
options.case: An engineer may enjoy it, but a layout that follows a strut network is slow to read.
options.kept: One underlying data set drives every view.
options.risk: The structure becomes the subject instead of the work.

options.label: Night Wake
options.lineage: bioluminescent plankton lighting a wake at night
options.thesis: A black page where the pointer draws glowing trails that fade.
options.viewport: Dark field, name in thin glowing letters, trails following the cursor.
options.case: This is the old attempt again: an effect first, on a dark page, with no tie to robots or Saltillo.
options.kept: Motion only as an answer to the visitor's own movement.
options.risk: Effects before content, the exact failure of the last version.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The portfolio as a scrolling green-on-black terminal transcript.
options.viewport: A blinking cursor and typed lines listing projects.
options.case: The most common developer-portfolio costume, and it shuts out web clients.
options.kept: States announce themselves in the page's own voice.
options.risk: Seen on thousands of developer sites.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The clean developer portfolio everyone recognises, built carefully.
canonCard.viewport: Name, one-line role and two buttons, then a grid of project cards, about, and contact.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other portfolios by design.
